findings.claim: S3 getDataWithMetadata takes the length from the GetObject response, which under the default multipart client is part 1's response, so any object uploaded in parts reports its first part's size (8 MiB) instead of its full size.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, on S3 with storage.s3.multipartEnabled at its default (true), a complex obs over 8 MiB gets ComplexData length 8388608; legacyui's ComplexObsServlet sends that as Content-Length and Tomcat's IdentityOutputFilter discards everything after it, so the download is silently truncated with a 200 and no error anywhere.
findings.evidence: SDK 2.32.13 sources (version from bom/pom.xml awsSdkS3Version, confirmed by dependency:list): DownloadObjectHelper.downloadObject splits the transformer and MultipartDownloaderSubscriber requests partNumber=1..n; InputStreamResponseTransformer uses AsyncResponseTransformer's default split, whose SplittingTransformer forwards only the first onResponse to the upstream transformer; DEFAULT_MIN_PART_SIZE = 8 MiB. Ran a throwaway JUnit test driving the real MultipartS3AsyncClient.create(...) over a fake S3AsyncClient that answers partNumber GETs as S3 does (part Content-Length, Content-Range bytes a-b/total, partsCount): getDataWithMetadata returned all 20 bytes but length=8, HEAD-based getMetadata=20; control without multipart: length=20. With the suggested getObjectLength applied: 20 in both. Suggested code is spotless-stable (spotless:apply left it byte-identical; positive control: a deliberately mangled line in it was reformatted). legacyui-omod 2.1.0-SNAPSHOT ComplexObsServlet bytecode: ComplexData.getLength() -> setHeader("Content-Length"). tomcat-coyote 9.0.106 IdentityOutputFilter.doWrite drops bytes past Content-Length. S3StorageServiceIT never calls getDataWithMetadata. End to end against containers (cached images, real S3StorageService, 20 MiB object saved through saveData): LocalStack 3.8.1 with multipart=true -> bytesRead=20971520, dwm.length=8388608, HEAD length=20971520; multipart=false control -> 20971520. With the suggested getObjectLength applied: LocalStack multipart=true -> 20971520. S3Mock 4.5.0 (what S3StorageServiceIT uses) reports 20971520 even with multipart on, so the IT cannot catch this.

findings.claim: read() only falls back to the legacy location on NoSuchFileException, but a pre-2.8 file whose title is long and non-ASCII percent-encodes to a name over 255 bytes, so the current-location stat fails with a plain FileSystemException ('File name too long') and the legacy file is never tried.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, on any instance that has saved a complex obs since 2.8 (so storageDir/complex_obs exists), legacy obs whose title is about 36+ Cyrillic or 24+ Ethiopic letters (with a .pdf extension) throw on every read where master returned them, because the encoded current-location name exceeds NAME_MAX and the exception is not NoSuchFileException.
findings.evidence: Pre-2.8 naming read at df94143ec (80b4411f8^) AbstractHandler.getOutputFileToWrite: titleWithoutExtension + "_" + uuid + extension; BinaryDataHandler there set valueComplex "<name> file |<name>". BaseStorageService.encodeKey URL-encodes (non-ASCII byte -> %XX). Throwaway test (legacy file at appdata/complex_obs/<title>_<uuid>.pdf, key complex_obs/<name>, as parseDataKey produces): on PR head with storageDir/complex_obs present, cyr36 and amh24 throw java.nio.file.FileSystemException ... File name too long; known-good cyr35/amh23/ascii36 read. Without storageDir/complex_obs the parent lookup fails first (ENOENT) and all read, which is why the condition matters; new obs keys are complex_obs/<timestamp...> per BaseStorageService.newKey, so the dir exists on any instance that has saved one. Same test in a master worktree: all five read. Suggested read() applied: all five read; LocalStorageServiceTest, AbstractHandlerTest, TextHandlerTest, BinaryStreamHandlerTest, ImageHandlerTest: 88 tests green; spotless:apply only removed the now-unused NoSuchFileException import.

findings.evidence: Copied the PR's ImageHandlerTest into a master worktree: getObs_shouldNotThrowWhenTheObsDirGlobalPropertyHasNoValue fails there with NullPointerException ('this.pattern' is null, from replaceFirst(null)); getObs_shouldFallBackToLegacyFilenameWhenTheFileIsMissing passes on master. No reviewer thread asked for the guard.
findings.body: Could this guard and `getObs_shouldNotThrowWhenTheObsDirGlobalPropertyHasNoValue` go in their own ticket? Master throws the same NPE here when the obs dir property is unset (that test fails on master too), so it's a separate fix from the I/O counts, and keeping it out leaves less to verify here. Nothing breaks with it in.

findings.claim: S3 getData duplicates getDataWithMetadata's GetObject call and 404 translation; it can delegate.
findings.evidence: Applied the one-line delegation: compiles, spotless:apply leaves it unchanged, and through the fake S3 client getData returned all 20 bytes. ibacher's comment id 3990739410 in the conversation snapshot asked for the same de-duplication in LocalStorageService.
findings.body:
This can just delegate to `getDataWithMetadata`, which repeats the same GetObject call and 404 translation (the duplication ibacher flagged in `LocalStorageService`, [comment](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-core/pull/6535#discussion_r3990739410)), since the GET already carries the headers:

```suggestion
		return getDataWithMetadata(key).data();
```

verdict: Not ready to merge: on S3 with the default multipart client the combined read reports an 8 MiB length for larger objects, which silently truncates downloads (F1), and legacy obs with long non-ASCII titles stop loading on local storage (F2).
what_i_swept: Step 1: PR body, TRUNK-6682 snapshot, full conversation snapshot; checked every prior thread against the head (greptile default-method, URI_VIEW, fallback narrowing, formatting; ibacher's internal-helpers, ordering comment, NoSuchFileException docs, BinaryDataHandler, APIException; my earlier ImageHandler early-return and call-count threads all resolved at head, so silent; the @since thread's maintenance-lines sub-point survives -> F7). The truncation is established from legacyui-omod's ComplexObsServlet bytecode (sets Content-Length from ComplexData.getLength()) and Tomcat 9.0.106's IdentityOutputFilter source, and the wrong length itself was reproduced end to end on LocalStack.
